questions.q: What is mirroring in a negotiation?
a: Repeating the other person's words as a question
Copying their posture and gestures
Repeating your own offer until accepted
Matching their tone and speaking speed
questions.why: Lesson 1 defines mirroring as repeating what someone says, phrased as a question.

questions.q: Why does mirroring help in a negotiation?
a: It makes the other person feel similar and more trusting
It confuses them into lowering their price
It hides your real intentions from them
It speeds up the conversation
questions.why: Lesson 1 says mirroring makes people feel you are alike, which builds trust and encourages them to talk.

questions.q: What does labeling the other side's emotions do?
a: It calms them and engages rational thinking
It proves that you agree with them
It forces them to make a quick offer
It shows you are not willing to listen
questions.why: Lesson 2 says labeling feelings calms people and brain scans show it activates the rational part of the brain.

questions.q: Why does the author say never to split the difference?
a: Their stated demand may not be what they want
Compromise always costs you more money
The other side will respect you less
Deadlines make compromise impossible
questions.why: Lesson 3 argues people hide thoughts, so giving them what they ask for may not solve the real problem.

questions.q: What did the Haitian kidnapping case reveal about deadlines?
a: They were flexible, tied to the kidnappers' weekend plans
They were fixed by the police and never moved
They were set by the family and could not change
They mattered less than the ransom amount
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the author saw the kidnappers cared about partying, so their Friday deadlines were not serious.
